groups.problem: The postMessage receiver validates origins using substring containment instead of exact origin equality.
groups.rationale: All three identify the same discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) check and propose validating the sender against the Discourse origin.

groups.problem: The resize message uses the full referrer URL as targetOrigin instead of extracting its origin.
groups.rationale: Each reports the same postMessage argument and the resulting failure to deliver resize messages.

groups.problem: Feed importing calls scrub on potentially nil item content, aborting imports for description-only entries.
groups.rationale: Both identify the same nil dereference and suggest falling back to description or an empty string. S4's additional title handling appears only in its proposed fix.

problems: Feed and article fetching lack SSRF safeguards against internal destinations and unsafe redirects.
Feed and article fetching lack timeouts, allowing slow responses to occupy workers.
uncoveredProblems: Remote fetching lacks SSRF destination and redirect validation.
Remote fetching lacks timeouts to bound worker occupation.

problems: The resize message uses the full referrer URL as targetOrigin, causing delivery failures and alleged referrer exposure.
The targetOrigin construction does not handle a nil referrer.
uncoveredProblems: The resize message does not guard against a nil referrer.

problems: Remote article fetching leaves network and OpenURI failures unhandled.
URL absolutization leaves URI parsing failures unhandled for malformed URLs that pass the prefix check.
uncoveredProblems: Remote article fetching can terminate retrieval jobs with unhandled network exceptions.
URL absolutization can raise unhandled URI parsing exceptions.

problems: The feed_key method computes a cache key that is never used.
Feed polling fetches unchanged feeds without conditional requests or a cache check.
uncoveredProblems: The feed_key method is unused dead computation.
Feed polling lacks caching or conditional fetching to avoid redundant downloads.
